The image shows a leaf with a large irregular reddish-brown/brownish-orange necrotic area covering most of the leaf surface, with healthy green tissue remaining on the right side. The affected area is extensive with an irregular boundary.

Key observations:
- Large irregular brownish-orange discoloration on the upper leaf surface
- Not discrete circular spots with defined rings (rules out Brown_Eye_Spot, Berry_Blotch)
- No visible mining trails or pale yellow patterns (rules out Miner)
- Not discrete circular dark spots (rules out Phoma)
- The reddish-brown/orange coloration and large irregular pattern is consistent with rust infection in an advanced stage where "leaves eventually dry up and turn brown"
- The irregular shape on the upper surface matches "irregular shaped spots on upper leaf surfaces" described for Rust

The extensive brownish-orange discoloration covering a large portion of the leaf, with an irregular boundary between diseased and healthy tissue, is most consistent with Rust (Hemileia vastatrix), which causes leaves to progressively dry up and turn brown after initial yellow-orange lesion development.
